title: Act II, Scene IV

teacherSummary.text: Ross and an Old Man describe unnatural events: darkness by day, a falcon killed by a 'mousing owl', and Duncan's horses breaking loose and eating each other. Macduff reports that the princes are suspected of bribing the grooms, that Macbeth has been named king and has gone to Scone to be invested, and that Duncan's body has been carried to Colmekill. Macduff will not go to Scone but home to Fife.

context.history: The idea of a 'great chain of being' held that a king's murder disordered nature; Holinshed's chronicle supplied the omens of the horses and the darkness.

significance: The omens turn the murder into a cosmic crime. Macduff's quiet refusal to attend the coronation is the first sign of resistance.
